plan.expected_behavior: Exercise decisions become less optimistic and less sensitive to extreme high-volatility targets. The largest expected benefit is on the one-dimensional deep-out-of-the-money high-volatility put, which dominates the score; the stronger-ridge fallback should preserve the near-ATM two-dimensional max-call performance. Runtime remains far below 30 seconds.
plan.failure_condition: Reject the intervention if, under matched seeds and evaluation paths, its mean discounted payoff is below the unchanged parent, or if sparse positive-payoff folds repeatedly trigger unstable coefficients or materially delay valuable exercise.
plan.implementation: Keep features(), model.npz, and predict() unchanged. In fit(), use deterministic 4-fold splits from seed. At each date, for ridge values {1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1e-1}, train standardized ridge models on each fold's complement using only rows with payoff > 0; generate held-out continuation predictions and update pathwise cash_flow solely from these out-of-fold predictions. Select the ridge value maximizing the resulting mean realized cash_flow, preferably with a one-standard-error tie-break toward stronger regularization. After completing the selected cross-fitted backward pass, rerun backward induction and, at every date, fit the serialized coefficient on all positive-payoff paths against the selected pass's downstream out-of-fold cash_flow targets. Use the existing all-path fit only when fewer than max(20, 2*feature_count) positive-payoff rows exist.
plan.mechanism: Replace the in-sample backward regression with cross-fitted, in-the-money ridge LSMC. Out-of-fold continuation estimates prevent each path's noisy future payoff from influencing its own stopping decision, while restricting regression to positive-payoff paths concentrates the 256 samples on the exercise boundary. This should reduce look-ahead exercise errors and increase out-of-sample discounted payoff.
